content: coffee A controlled blast on a movie set near London’s O2 arena ignited a fire that consumed a van and harmed a car and a lorry. Fire crews were summoned to an open‑air lot on Dock Road in Silvertown just before eight on Saturday evening. After about an hour, the flames were brought under control by roughly twenty‑five firefighters, and no one was hurt. Officials said the blaze stemmed from a pre‑arranged filming activity close to the venue, which will host shows by Niall Horan and Texas later in the week. The London Fire Brigade posted on X that the fire in the Silvertown yard is now contained, noting that the van was destroyed and most of the car and lorry suffered damage, with no injuries reported. They added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the set that spread unexpectedly, and crews worked swiftly to douse it and will stay on site for the rest of the night. The yard lies near the Thames cable‑car crossing, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed they are aware of reports of explosions heard close to the O2 in Greenwich.
